observations: 100 successful resource-A observations (5 collection-neutral intents x 20 identifiers across items/tags) were induced into exactly 5 parameter-slot mechanisms, one per intent, each with confidence 0.956522 (Beta(2,1) posterior mean 0.9565217 x leave-one-out consistency 1.0).

Each induced mechanism exposes a slot for the varying collection plus the per-task identifier, and the list mechanism additionally exposes q and limit; every durable template contains ${auth_token} and no bearer-token literal.

The literal incumbent-style mechanisms distilled from the same evidence embed the literal resource-A bearer token in their persisted action_template, expose no parameter slots, and carry the hardcoded confidence 0.5.

On 150 resource-B transfer tasks whose identifiers never appear in the induction evidence, the treatment executed a bound mechanism on 150/150 tasks, with binding accuracy 1.0, postcondition pass 1.0 and kernel verification pass 1.0.
The treatment used a cold fallback on 0 of 150 resource-B tasks and issued exactly 1.0 HTTP request per task in every family.
Every resolution the treatment issued on resource B was EXECUTABLE; no EXPLORE or UNKNOWN resolution occurred on a transfer task.
60 negative probes (40 unlearned-intent probes over 2 collections and 2 roles, plus 20 prefix-collision probes) all resolved UNKNOWN with 0 false accepts.

The null control (intent labels permuted across all observations) induced 4 mechanisms whose mechanism success rate on resource B was 0.0, with abstention precision 1.0 and cost equal to B-COLD (ratio 1.0).

The positive control on held-out resource-A identifiers reached mechanism success 1.0 and binding accuracy 1.0 at 1.0 HTTP request per task, while the B-COLD arm on those same tasks also cost 1.0 request per task.
The documented-executor cold arm (B-COLD-DOC) achieved end-to-end success 1.0 on the query family and 0.0 on both crud-write and crud-read, for 0.333 overall.

The forced literal replay arm was given a valid working credential and still achieved binding accuracy 0.0 and mechanism success 0.0 on resource B; its end-to-end success of 1.0 came entirely from cold fallback.

The committed incumbent kernel has no distill_parameterized, reports distill confidence 0.5 against min_confidence 0.8, resolves same-intent to EXPLORE and paraphrased intent to UNKNOWN, and produced executable fraction 0.0 with 0 HTTP requests on the resource-B probe.
validity_notes: Substrate substitution, disclosed: prereg 8 named Flask and this environment has no flask, so the substrate is stdlib http.server on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port. The API surface, status codes, auth failures, session-scoped bodies and ETag/304 behaviour were verified by a self-test recorded before the arms ran.

Representation loss, disclosed: the training corpus contains only items and tags, so the collection slot's only observed values are {items, tags}. Transfer to products is an extrapolation to a third, unobserved value of that slot, and the measured success on products is out-of-support generalization rather than interpolation.

The list training actions repeat their (q, limit) pairs within each collection, so two resource-A observations per intent share an evidence id. The observation count is 100 but the distinct-evidence count is lower; this does not affect the leave-one-out result, which reached 1.0 consistency.

Cost dynamic-range limitation, disclosed: on this substrate cold exploration already costs 1.0 HTTP request per read and per query, so there is no per-task saving for the treatment to amortize its 100-request induction bill against on those families. The 0.85 amortization target is unreachable there for any system, including a correct one.

D6 has the same limitation on the positive-control task set, where B-COLD also costs 1.0 request per task, so the cost_ratio <= 0.50 half of the positive control cannot be met by any system on this substrate. Its correctness and binding halves are 1.0.

The treatment's confidence is a single value (0.956522) across all 150 executed transfer tasks, so the treatment ECE is a single-bin quantity and carries little information about calibration resolution; the pooled all-arm ECE (0.019763 over n=550) is the more informative calibration number and is reported alongside.

The 150 transfer tasks are 3 intents x 50 tasks, so per-family success rates are exact counts out of 50 and the family-stratified bootstrap CI is degenerate at [1.0, 1.0]. No population-level generalization beyond these task constructions is claimed.
No model, browser, network egress or external dataset was used. This is a controlled harness measurement of the kernel's inheritance path, not an end-to-end web agent evaluation.

Three product-code defects were found and fixed during execution, before the reported run: string-only slot alignment that could not represent integer-valued query parameters, verbatim copying of a constant Authorization header into a durable template, and volatile session metadata being promoted to a hard precondition. Each fix is covered by a unit test in tests/test_kernel.py; they are product behaviour changes inside the lane's authorized code root and are part of what was measured.

The D5 denominator is restricted to the three baselines prereg 4.2 declares and matched on the prereg 4.3 task-level success_rate, with an additional requirement that the baseline be competent (end-to-end success >= 0.80) in every family. Both restrictions make the D5 test harder for the treatment, not easier.
unresolved: Whether the economic failure is intrinsic to parameter inheritance or an artifact of this substrate's low cold-baseline cost is not settled here. Measured break-even is 254 transfer tasks on crud-write and unreachable on crud-read and query; a substrate with a genuine discovery cost would be needed to separate the two.

The D6 cost criterion is not discriminating on this substrate and no substitute was substituted for it. A follow-up needs either a substrate with real discovery cost or a prereg that treats the cost half of the positive control as expected-to-fail.

Parameter inheritance beyond one collection dimension is untested: the induced slots cover collection, id, q, limit and auth_token only. Whether the same machinery spans schemas with different field names, nested bodies or multi-step flows is unknown.

Whether the mechanism abstains correctly when a slot is bound outside the observed support is untested in the failure direction; this run only shows that it does not abstain and does succeed on a third collection value.

Repair on binding or execution failure (C-DELTA-REPAIR) was explicitly out of scope and remains unmeasured. The fallback path used here is harness-level cold exploration, not a kernel repair capability.

Staleness and freshness (C-FRESHNESS) were not exercised. The mechanism records evidence-scope metadata including observed_distinct_identifiers=2 for the list intent, which reflects the repeated list actions rather than a freshness assessment.
